does: Cuts food into small, loose pieces, not exact cubes, so that they spread through rice, a filling or a sauce.
how: Trim the food, take out any bone or tough stem, and slice it first if it is wide.
Cut the slices across into small, rough pieces.
Try to keep the pieces about the same size, so that they cook together.
Gather the pieces in a bowl as you go.

cues.text: The pieces are small and similar in size, and can be scattered with a spoon.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting the pieces large, so that they cannot spread evenly through the rice.
mistakes.fix: Cut them about as small as a grain of rice.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting soft food on a crowded board, so that it is squashed.
mistakes.fix: Use a sharp knife and a clear board.

variant_of.differs: The pieces are small but cut by eye and not to an exact cube, since they only need to blend into rice or a filling.
The pieces are small and loose, cut to spread through rice, a filling or a sauce, so the exact shape still does not matter.
